segments.narration: Two billion years ago, Earth built its own nuclear reactor. In 1972, French scientists testing uranium ore from Gabon found that the fuel had already been burned.
Key isotopes of uranium-235 were missing, leaving behind the exact chemical byproduct found in modern nuclear waste. It looked like an ancient power plant.
How could atomic fuel be consumed before humans even existed? Geologists began analyzing the surrounding rock.
They discovered an impossible coincidence. Two billion years ago, natural uranium was far more concentrated, and seeping groundwater naturally slowed neutrons down, igniting spontaneous fission.
Whenever it boiled, steam escaped and shut the reaction off until it cooled, running a self-regulating nuclear reactor for hundreds of thousands of years.
